stage1.impression: The fir-lined niche with two lit speakers on oak plinths makes a clear, warm composition, but it reads as a CG showroom, not a photograph: the floor and tub chairs are flat untextured planes, the speakers' white batts glare near white so the cabinets read as clear boxes of grey parts instead of smoked acrylic, and the foreground is taken up by a soft salmon-pink block with two featureless white discs that look like blown plastic. It is a generic, empty demo room, not a specific place a design magazine would publish; there is no sign of life and no concrete, steel or beam detail to place it.

blocking_9: Foreground oak table and Orb lamps read as a real oak top and tinted acrylic lamps, not a salmon block and white discs: the Orbs' frosted liners below lum 170, the oak top's r/g ratio under 1.3
Speakers read as smoked tinted acrylic at a glance: the white batts behind the front panel at or below lum 190, not 240, and visible tint in the cabinet
Floor and tub chairs show material at 1:1 (velvet nap, floor grain or polish with soft reflections of the niche) instead of flat planes
The shell shows: board-formed concrete, a fir beam or blackened steel reads somewhere in the frame, so it is this bar and not a generic room
One sign of life in sharp focus in the mid-ground (glass, record and sleeve, coat), not only off-frame
The right foreground chair (740-1095, 530-800) holds detail: crush under 5 %

defects.what: Foreground oak table reads as flat salmon-pink plastic (r 160, g 114, b 93), out of focus, with no grain
Orb lamp reads as a blown featureless white disc (median lum 213, neutral grey-white, no tint)
Second Orb lamp cut by the frame edge, a white disc (median lum 212) that pulls the eye out of the frame
Left speaker's top batt clips nearly white (median 241) and reads as a lit white box, not behind smoked acrylic
Left speaker's horn and cabinet read as clear/grey, the smoke tint not legible; front panel reflection is flat
Right speaker's resin horn shows a hard, cartoonish starburst reflection of the rig, plastic-looking
Floor is a flat dark plane (lum range 29) with no texture, reflection or falloff from the niche
Tub chair is a smooth untextured CG shell, near crushed in its lower half (median lum 8, crush 9.5 %)
Screen on the left wall reads as a washed grey poster, a distracting large light-grey shape
Ceiling and upper shell are empty dark; no beam, concrete or steel reads, so the room is generic
Fir niche boards are uniform and repeat; no checks or variation; the niche looks like a showroom booth
Second table edge at right, cut by the frame, with a stray bright edge

changes.problem: The foreground is dominated by an out-of-focus salmon table and two blown Orb discs that read as plastic and pull the eye off the altar.

evidence.measured: median lum 122, r 160 g 114 b 93; Orb discs median 212-213, neutral white

change.to: position about [12.6, 2.2, 1.15], target [16.6, 3.0, 1.05], 35 mm, f/5.6 focused at [15.5, 3.0, 1.0]: the near table either fully out of frame or one whole table with its Orb sitting in the lower-left third, not cut by the edge

changes.expected: The altar pair larger and central; no half-cut white disc at the frame edge; foreground reads as one deliberate oak table with a lamp, or none.

changes.problem: The speakers' batts glare near white, so the smoked cabinets read as clear boxes and the hero's tint is lost.

change.to: 30 W, cone 18 deg, aimed 150 mm lower so it grazes the cabinet front and plinth rather than the batt top; add a rim from behind via the lit niche strip 0.07 -> 0.12 so the smoked edges glow

changes.expected: Batts read soft grey behind the smoked panel; cabinet edges glow; speaker region still bright enough to lead.

changes.problem: The Orb lamps read as blown neutral discs instead of tinted acrylic with a frosted liner.

evidence.measured: median lum 213, r 213 g 213 b 210 (no tint)

change.to: 0.10 W, glow 0.003, so the smoke tint over the liner shows

changes.expected: Orbs glow warm grey-smoke with a visible gradient, under lum 170.

changes.problem: The floor is a dead flat plane, so the room has no ground and the niche's light has nowhere to fall.

evidence.measured: lum range 28.8, median 17, no visible texture or reflection

change.to: satin polish (roughness about 0.3) with a subtle grain/patina, so the plinths and lit niche leave a soft streak reflection

changes.expected: A soft warm reflection of the niche falls toward the camera; floor shows tonal variation.

changes.problem: The right tub chair and right side fall into crushed black with no material read.

change.to: exposure 4.9; one downlight aimed onto the right chair's arm and seat at 50 W, so the velvet nap catches a highlight

changes.expected: Velvet nap legible on the chair's top edge; shadows deep but not empty.

changes.problem: No sign of life near the altar; the room reads as an empty showroom.

evidence.measured: seen: no glass, record or coat visible in focus

change.from: round 39 props: 1 rocks, 1 votives (none in frame)
change.to: the record and sleeve leaning on the right plinth, a coat over the near tub chair, a half-drunk glass on the near table, all inside the frame

changes.expected: One or two lived-in details read in the mid-ground.

changes.problem: The ceiling and shell are empty black, so concrete, beams and steel never read and the place is generic.

change.setting: haze and a spill on the shell
change.to: haze 0.006; let the niche's spill (or a 6 W grazer from the record wall spots) graze the beam above the niche and the concrete on the left so the board marks read

changes.expected: A beam and board-formed concrete visible in the upper frame at low key.

changes.problem: The left-wall screen reads as a washed grey poster competing with the altar.
changes.expected: The screen sits back as a dim image, under the speakers in brightness.

out_of_scope.request: Make the smoked tint of the speaker cabinets and horn read stronger in the material itself
out_of_scope.why: The speakers' colour is fixed by the card; only light and exposure can bring it out (c2).

out_of_scope.request: Replace the uniform fir board pattern in the niche with more varied boards with checks and nail holes
out_of_scope.why: The niche's material is fixed room design; only its finish (stain/variation) may change, and whether board variation counts as finish should be decided by the owner.

out_of_scope.request: Give the tub chairs a more specific pedigree silhouette
out_of_scope.why: The seats are fixed room design.
